title: Normalisation: why, 1NF to 3NF, creating the tables

learning_objectives.text: list the normalisation rules for the first, second and third normal forms
normalize a database to the 3rd normal form
create a database with multiple tables for a new system

lesson_objectives.all: explain why databases are normalised and state the rules of 1NF, 2NF and 3NF
lesson_objectives.most: normalise a given table to 3NF and identify primary and foreign keys
lesson_objectives.some: normalise a new scenario to 3NF, justify each step by its dependencies and write CREATE TABLE statements with keys

descriptors: names and explains update, insertion and deletion anomalies with examples

assessment_criteria.criterion: List the rules of the normal forms
descriptors: states the rules of 1NF, 2NF and 3NF in order
removes repeating groups and chooses a key (1NF)
moves partial dependencies to new tables (2NF)
moves transitive dependencies to new tables and links them with foreign keys (3NF)

assessment_criteria.criterion: Create a database with multiple tables
descriptors: creates tables in the right order
writes CREATE TABLE with PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY

learners_can: explain cause and effect (because the data is repeated, …)
describe a process in steps (first, then, finally)
justify a design decision with subject terms
phrases: This table is not in 1NF because …
… depends only on part of the key, so …
… depends on …, which is not a key, so …
The final tables are …, linked by …

values.action: Groups normalise a messy real-life table step by step and check that every fact is stored only once.
Random pairs and groups share one laptop, agree on dependencies and design the tables together.
Learners connect normalisation with their earlier ERDs and data dictionaries and see how the design stage builds a real database.

cross_curricular: Mathematics: dependencies and sets; splitting data without losing it.
English: describing a process and justifying decisions.
Business: why shops, clinics and schools need consistent data.
ict: ICT Practice Platform, Lessons section: theory as slides, live votes and tasks, random pairs and groups on shared laptops.
Practice questions with automatic feedback; results visible to the teacher live.
Client cards with unnormalised tables on the learners' screens for the group task.
previous_learning: Basic concepts of a database (tables, keys, data types), ERDs (entities, relationships, link tables) and the data dictionary.
safety: Move to the group's laptop calmly; keep bags and cables off the floor.
Short screen break between the two halves of the lesson.

support: Key words with definitions on the title slide; sentence frames for each step.
The club register worked example on the slides before the group task.
The group task has labelled boxes for 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and SQL.
Random mixed-ability groups with roles: leader, writer, checker, presenter.
stretch: Explain why a table with a single-field key is automatically in 2NF.
Explain one drawback of normalisation (more joins).
Write a SELECT with a JOIN that rebuilds the original report from the 3NF tables.

assessment: Live results of every task on the teacher's slide; misconceptions are discussed at once.
Together votes check understanding before the next step opens.
The group's normalisation is checked by the teacher with feedback during the lesson.
Exit ticket (marked automatically) checks the lesson objectives.
Practice results count towards SAU points.

blocks.title: Hook: one phone number, 40 rows
blocks.teacher: Shows the objectives and a flat school register where a teacher's phone is repeated in 40 rows. Asks what happens when it changes. Learners vote; leads into redundancy and anomalies.
blocks.learners: Vote on their laptops and explain.

Some rows keep the old number

Orders(OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerID, CustomerName, Email, ProductID, ProductName, Price, Quantity). An order has many products.
Appointments(AppointmentID, Date, PatientID, PatientName, Phone, DoctorID, DoctorName, Speciality). A doctor has many appointments.

live_tasks.text: How is a many-to-many relationship stored in a database?

options.content: With a link table holding both primary keys

live_tasks.title: Spot the anomaly
live_tasks.text: A teacher's phone number is stored in 40 rows of a flat table. It changes, and only 39 rows are updated. Which problem is this?

scheme.explanation: The same fact is stored many times, so a change must be made everywhere — normalisation stores it once.

live_tasks.title: Which normal form is broken?
live_tasks.text: `OrderLines(OrderID, ProductID, ProductName, Quantity)`, key (OrderID, ProductID). ProductName depends only on ProductID. Which form is broken?

scheme.explanation: A non-key field depends on only part of the composite key: a partial dependency breaks 2NF.

live_tasks.title: Create order
live_tasks.text: Tables `Members`, `Classes` and the link table `Bookings` (with foreign keys to both). Which must be created last?

scheme.explanation: A foreign key can only refer to a table that already exists.

live_tasks.title: Database designers: normalise a client's table
live_tasks.text: Your group gets an unnormalised table (see your card). Normalise it to 3NF and plan the database.

fields.label: 1NF: the table(s) with atomic values and the primary key (underline it or write PK)
2NF: the tables after removing partial dependencies (or explain why it is already in 2NF)
3NF: the final tables with primary keys and foreign keys
Name one anomaly the original table had and explain how your design removes it
CREATE TABLE for the table with a foreign key (fields, types, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY)

scheme.mark_scheme:
1NF: repeating groups removed, atomic values, suitable (composite) key (2)
2NF: partial dependencies removed into their own tables, or correct reason it is already in 2NF (2)
3NF: transitive dependency removed; every table has a PK; foreign keys link the tables (2)
Anomaly named and linked to the client's data, with how the design removes it (2)
CREATE TABLE with suitable types, PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY … REFERENCES (2)

points.criterion: 1NF atomic values and repeating groups removed

scheme.model_answer: Sports club. 1NF: Bookings(MemberID, ClassID, MemberName, Phone, ClassName, TrainerID, TrainerName, Day), key (MemberID, ClassID). 2NF: Members(MemberID, MemberName, Phone); Classes(ClassID, ClassName, TrainerID, TrainerName, Day); Bookings(MemberID, ClassID). 3NF: Trainers(TrainerID, TrainerName); Classes(ClassID, ClassName, Day, TrainerID FK). Anomaly: a trainer's name was stored on every booking — renaming meant changing many rows (update anomaly); now it is stored once in Trainers. SQL: CREATE TABLE Classes (ClassID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ClassName VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, Day VARCHAR(10), TrainerID INTEGER, FOREIGN KEY (TrainerID) REFERENCES Trainers(TrainerID));

options.content: Atomic values, no repeating groups, a primary key
Every table has a foreign key
